children: Oracle (OCL) shares rose more than 9% on Wednesday as the company reaffirmed its fiscal 2027 guidance and provided a long-term outlook at its financial analyst day.
For the remainder of fiscal 2027, Oracle expects earnings to be $8.10 per share, with revenue at $90B. Analysts had expected $8.14 per share in earnings and $90.45B in revenue.
At the investor event, Oracle said it expects a 35% compound annual growth rate between fiscal 2026 and fiscal 2030, with revenue hitting $225B or more by fiscal 2030.

The company also provided updates on its profitability and free cash flow. Oracle expects peak capital spending to be between fiscal 2027 and fiscal 2028, though spending is expected to slow down in fiscal 2029, with the company ultimately hitting $30B in free cash flow in fiscal 2029.

In addition, Oracle said it only expects to raise $20B from capital markets (excluding refinancing) between fiscal 2027 and fiscal 2030, with $10B coming from equity and $10B from tapping the debt markets. Oracle added that vendor financing, customer-provided hardware, and prepayments should help reduce upfront cash requirements, Oracle added.
